newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury task force on tax may not be last.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury task force on tax may not be last.

text.p: The task force on tax and benefits to be headed by Barclays Plc chief executive Martin Taylor is a model that could be used by the Treasury to examine other areas of policy, government officials said on Monday.
They said the new government saw no reason to be embarrassed at all in drawing on expert help from outside to advise on the formulation of policy.
"Don't be surprised if it's done in this (the Treasury) and other departments," one official said.
Taylor, who will report to Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, is the second leading businessmen to be co-opted by Prime Minister Tony Blair's government.
British Petroleum's Sir David Simon has been named as minister for competitiveness in Europe.
Officials said Labour had developed good relations with business while it was in opposition and it wanted to build on them.
